exposure: long-term treatment for SCD (hydroxyurea and/or transfusion programme)
cohort: The study included all singleton pregnancy-related hospital discharges from 2013 to 2020 in women aged 15-55 (n = 5,752,080) from the French national health database, with 1022 births to women with SCD.
finding: Pregnancies in women with sickle cell disease, both untreated and long-term treated, were associated with significantly higher risks of maternal complications (pre-eclampsia, pulmonary embolism, postpartum haemorrhage) and perinatal complications (preterm birth, adverse neonatal outcomes, congenital abnormalities) compared to pregnancies without SCD.
mod_finding: Pregnancies with sickle cell disease were significantly more likely to involve caesarean sections (52.8% vs. 18.2%) compared to pregnancies without SCD.
